pr_title: feat(trace-viewer): display text attachments in ui mode
pr_body: Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/30976 Displays text attachment contents in UI mode
pr_comments:
@alvaromartmart Thank you for the PR! We discussed this with the team, and came up with a few comments/suggestions:

- Could you please attach a screenshot that illustrates the UI implemented in the latest commit?
- We feel like the proposed UI is not very intuitive and we could bring more clarity and structure into it. Perhaps we can show `no preview available` for other attachments when there is at least a single preview? Otherwise the UI looks confusing to me.
- Looking at the code, multi-line attachments will be rendered as a single line.
- Perhaps we should make this more like network request/response body preview? [See here](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/packages/trace-viewer/src/ui/networkResourceDetails.tsx#L91) for the code pointer.
- In addition to `text/plain`, we can preview many more [textual mime types](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/packages/playwright-core/src/utils/mimeType.ts#L21-L23).

> @alvaromartmart Thank you for the PR! We discussed this with the team, and came up with a few comments/suggestions: > Thank you for the feedback! > * Could you please attach a screenshot that illustrates the UI implemented in the latest commit? Here's a (WIP) screenshot with some annotations (more on them below) > * We feel like the proposed UI is not very intuitive and we could bring more clarity and structure into it. Perhaps we can show `no preview available` for other attachments when there is at least a single preview? Otherwise the UI looks confusing to me. Agree on the "no preview available". Additionally, I was wondering whether we should 1. Add some `hr` dividers between attachment to clearly tell them apart 2. Since attachments could be potentially big and the user not always be interested in looking at them, should we 2.a. render them by default 2.b. use an expansion panel, requiring user to expand them to see the contents 2.c. render by default files below some size threshold, otherwise use expansion panel > * Looking at the code, multi-line attachments will be rendered as a single line. They seem to render just fine, do you have a specific edge case in mind? > * Perhaps we should make this more like network request/response body preview? [See here](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/packages/trace-viewer/src/ui/networkResourceDetails.tsx#L91) for the code pointer. > * In addition to `text/plain`, we can preview many more [textual mime types](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/packages/playwright-core/src/utils/mimeType.ts#L21-L23). The screenshot above is the result of some experimentation using the `CodeMirrorWrapper` as you suggested. However I have some questions if we go this way: 3. should we infer when possible the `language` based on the mimeType to get the most accurate syntax highlighting? 4. should we always render as plain text, leveraging the styling of the `CodeMirrorWrapper` but skipping language-specific stuff? 5. attachments are displayed based on the `isTextualMimeType` utility now, but that utility includes `image/svg` - some users might expect the svg to be rendered instead of its source. Though this is likely an edge case that could be covered as a future iteration 😅

Ok so in [0eb57e7](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/31215/commits/0eb57e7774afc0ecad719b053c9e29dceab568c3) I placed the attachment in an expansion panel. You can see a demo here

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/assets/18287793/8970dda7-7182-4fd0-b575-fc5dba51a430

This way:
- attachments can still be downloaded as previously by clicking on their name
- attachments are not rendered by default, user needs to expand the panel
  - we could add an opt-in setting to expand attachments by default, but I guess it would be useful to collect user feedback first? Also I don't know if there are already ui mode specific settings

I think that can be done if needed in a future PR, if users ask for it.

Final question: since it's now using an expansion panel, maybe I can get rid of the `<hr>` delimiters, WDYT?

issue_context.title: [Feature]: UI mode - display text attachments as text, not links
issue_context.body:
### 🚀 Feature Request

I propose an enhancement to the UI mode of Playwright where text attachments (such as logs, plain text files, or text-based output) are displayed directly within the UI rather than as links that need to be clicked to view the content.

### Example

When running tests in UI mode, any text attachments generated by the tests would automatically be displayed in an expandable/collapsible section within the UI. This would allow users to quickly view relevant logs or output without the need to download and open separate files. For instance, if a test generates a log file as part of its output, the content of the log file would be displayed directly below the test result, allowing for quick review and debugging.

Current state
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/assets/45488285/a0a3c7d5-c6df-4314-8881-26fd4b2b5484)

Possible solution
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/assets/45488285/3d7c3e2c-99f1-4eb6-bf2b-955db5116abc)

### Motivation

This feature would improve the usability and efficiency of the Playwright UI mode by reducing the number of steps needed to access important information. Currently, users must click on links to download text attachments, which can be cumbersome and time-consuming, especially when dealing with multiple files or large logs. By displaying text attachments directly within the UI, users can more quickly identify and diagnose issues, leading to faster development and debugging cycles. This improvement aligns with the goal of making Playwright a more user-friendly and powerful tool for end-to-end testing.
comments: I'd like to work on this as a first contribution. I think I know where to start

This would be an awesome enhancement, could this also include the built-in generate html report as well? 
the stdout logs already show as text inline, but when I attach a text log file I have to download the zip file (same within the UI mode).
